target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path (`sandbox-exec-server/http.ts`) had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178` and other sibling spawn paths: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Before / after (processes.ts)**:

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Before / after (http.ts)**:

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — real sandbox exec-server WebSocket bridge**:

Both paths exercised through the production sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge. A child process writing 200 lines each to stdout/stderr is terminated mid-output; the bridge survives and a second process starts normally. The streaming HTTP subprocess path also survives socket closure mid-stream without crashing.

```text
$ npx vitest run --project extension-codex sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival

[14:53:42] EXEC-SERVER: Started on ws://127.0.0.1:59591/...
[14:53:42] EXEC-SERVER: WebSocket connected
[14:53:42] EXEC-SERVER: Spawning process "pipe-srv-101" with 200-line output
[14:53:42] EXEC-SERVER: Process "pipe-srv-101" spawned, pipes active
[14:53:42] EXEC-SERVER: Killing process "pipe-srv-101" mid-output
[14:53:43] EXEC-SERVER: Process closed. exitCode=1, chunks=9, closed=true
[14:53:43] EXEC-SERVER: Bridge survived -- WebSocket state is OPEN
[14:53:43] EXEC-SERVER: Starting second process "pipe-srv-102" ...
[14:53:43] EXEC-SERVER: Second process output: "bridge-survived"

[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: Started on ws://127.0.0.1:59593/...
[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: WebSocket connected
[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: Sending streaming HTTP request "http-pipe-201"
[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: Closing WebSocket mid-stream to trigger pipe errors
[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: WebSocket closed with code 1005
[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: Normal closure confirmed (code 1005) -- no crash
[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: Connecting new socket to verify bridge is still functional
[14:53:43] HTTP-BRIDGE: New connection established and ready
[14:53:44] HTTP-BRIDGE: Second process output: "http-bridge-survived"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

- The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178` for the general agent session exec path, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.
